proxy_language: Scythian (Eastern Iranian, Saka/Ossetic-derived reconstruction), with Thracian/Dacian as secondary substrate (Paleo-Balkan IE, very poorly attested)
proxy_rationale: The Scythian, Thracian and Dacian lands host three distinct IE languages. Scythian is Iranian and is reconstructed from Greek-transmitted names, Herodotus glosses and Ossetic (Digor/Iron) as its closest living descendant; Thracian and Dacian survive only as personal names, toponyms (-dava, -para, -bria), plant names and a few glosses, with no continuous texts. A court naming scheme is therefore best built on Old Iranian-style Scythian morphology (Ossetic-guided), flavored with Thracian/Dacian name elements. Link is weak: forms are mostly Greek-transcribed or reconstructed, and Thracian/Dacian phonology is highly uncertain.
phonology: Scythian (reconstructed/Ossetic-guided): vowels a, e, i, o, u plus long a; consonants p t k b d g, f x (h), s z, sh zh (š ž), c j (affricates), m n, r, l, w, y. Old Iranian *-ka- diminutive/adjective suffix, *-pa-/-pati- 'lord', *xshaya- 'rule'. Thracian/Dacian (Balkan IE, reconstructed from names): satem-like treatment is debated; Dacian -dava 'town' (*dhē-/*dhō- + -wa) and -bria 'town', -para 'town/village' are well-attested toponymic suffixes; Thracian names show -(k)entos, -mu(n)dos, -tralis, -poris 'son' (Thr. -poris = *-pora 'child'), -kenthos. Stress not recorded; no tone.
phonotactics: Prefer open and closed CV(C) syllables; consonant clusters allowed word-initially mainly as s+stop, st, sp, sk, xš, fr, tr, dr, kh; medial clusters rt, rd, rk, xš, st, sp, nd, nt, mb occur in attested names (Spargapeithes, Skyles, Ariapeithes, Saitaphernes, Kotys, Seuthes, Burebista, Decebalus, Zalmoxis). Words typically end in a vowel, -s (Greek nominative), -n, -r, or -a; Greek -os/-es endings are transmission artifacts and may be used for Hellenized court style but are optional. Avoid clusters of 3+ consonants outside s/x+stop+r. No voiced aspirates in the Scythian proxy; use plain b d g.
orthography: Standard scholarly Latinization of Greek-transmitted names with Iranian transliteration conventions: š ž č x are rendered as sh zh ch kh for game audit; use plain a e i o u, y as semivowel or vowel i, w for the labial glide, th ph kh only as Greek aspirates in Thracian-style names (Seuthes, Kotys). k not c for the velar stop. Hyphens separate compound members; apostrophes unused. Diacritics avoided.
morphology: Scythian (after Old Iranian/Ossetic): inflecting nouns with case; stems in -a, -i, -u, consonants; genitive in -ahya/-ahe (OIr) with Ossetic -i/-y; nominal compounds are dominant for names. Thracian/Dacian: names are mostly compounds of two lexical elements (e.g. Bi-thus, Sevtho-polis, Mucapor, Decebal) or single-stem names with suffixes -is, -as, -es, -ulus. Reduplication rare; no noun classes. Derivational suffixes: -ka (adjective/diminutive), -aina (feminine/collective), -dava/-para/-bria (place), -tar/-tara (agent, from OIr *-tar-).
compounding: Head-final determinative and possessive compounds, as in Old Iranian: modifier + head (e.g. Skythian *xshayathiya 'king'; Ariantas, Spargapeithes 'having a lofty/swelling... lord', *-peithes ~ *-pati- 'master'). 'X of Y' is best rendered as compound Y-X (genitive compound, Y-head last) or as juxtaposed genitive + head: Genitive Noun + Head Noun in the court register. 'Y-maker/-keeper' formed with agent suffix -tar/-pa/-pati (keeper/lord) after the object stem: e.g. horse-keeper = *aspa-pati. Place names: personal or tribal name + -dava ('town of X'), Dacian style. Linker vowel -a- between compound members (OIr *-a-), dropped before vowels.
noun_phrase_order: Adjective before noun (Old Iranian/Ossetic: adjective + noun), genitive before head noun in compounds, demonstratives before noun. Thracian/Dacian too presumed modifier-head from compounds.

attested_roots.gloss: horse (Scythian; cf. Aspa- in names, Ossetic jæfs-)
rule, king (Old Iranian, underlying Scythian royal titles)

worked_examples.name: Oiorpata-tuga
worked_examples.gloss: oior 'man' + pata 'slay' + tuga 'banner' (tuga is a placeholder Iranian-style root, flagged speculative)

notes: Scythian, Thracian and Dacian are separate languages; this proxy mixes them for a unified court register, which is a design choice, not attested practice. Thracian/Dacian phonology and meaning of most name elements is disputed; treat -dava/-para/-bria and -poris as safest. Many Greek-transmitted forms end in -s/-os (Hellenization); use or drop for style. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word since the language is not Goidelic.
